sentences.text: 2. It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.

There are no factors at play in [2023:RJ-JD:39399] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-13651/2023] the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor as well as learned counsel for the complainant oppose the bail application and submit that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4.
I have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material available on record.
The victim is a grown up lady aged about 25 years.
The incident took place on 10.09.2023 but the FIR came to be lodged on 21.09.2023.
There is no excuse as to why she kept mum for so long and did not disclose the fact that committing rape.
The matter is pending investigation, however, the investigation with regard to the petitioner has been completed.
He has been sent to the judicial custody.
There is no reason to allow further incarceration of the petitioner.

Looking to the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that the trial would still take a long time to conclude, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.

5. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the [2023:RJ-JD:39399] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-13651/2023] learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FARJAND ALI),J 234-Ashutosh/-
